headline: Species Declared Extinct in 1989 Found Alive in Ecuador
meta_description: Wildlife photographer Jay rediscovered the Mindo Harlequin Toad in Ecuador's cloud forest, a species thought wiped out by fungal disease 35 years ago.
summary_short: A species thought extinct for over three decades has been found alive in the Ecuadorian Andes—complete with tadpoles documented for the first time.
body:
A species declared extinct in 1989 has been rediscovered alive in the Ecuadorian Andes. Wildlife photographer and conservation storyteller Jay found survivors of the Mindo Harlequin Toad in a tiny section of the Mindo cloud forest, high in the mountains, reversing decades of assumed loss.

The toad had vanished after Chytridiomycosis, a fungal disease, swept through amphibian populations worldwide. The rediscovery brings unexpected hope—Jay's team not only found adult toads but also located tadpoles of the species, marking the first time these early life stages have been photographed and documented in history.

The find underscores how species once thought lost to extinction may still survive in remote refuges, and how dedicated fieldwork can reveal nature's resilience.
quick_facts: Mindo Harlequin Toad declared extinct in 1989
Rediscovered in Mindo cloud forest, Ecuadorian Andes
Found by wildlife photographer Jay and team
Species wiped out by Chytridiomycosis fungal disease
Tadpoles photographed and documented for the first time
